text: Much of the BLM literature has examined associations between a narrow bottom-line focus and employees’ conduct, voice, interpersonal experiences, and performance-related responses ( Babalola et al., 2020 ; Greenbaum et al., 2023 ). Emerging research has also linked BLM to innovation-related outcomes, often through risk, work values, or performance concerns ( Greenbaum et al., 2020 ; Luo et al., 2025 ). However, less attention has been given to whether BLM is associated with employees’ experience of meaning and social value at work ( Ren et al., 2018 ; Wang and Lee, 2023 ). This gap matters because innovation involves more than risk tolerance. Employees also need reasons to care about an idea, colleagues who can help advance it, and a sense that their efforts are consistent with the values emphasized by the organization ( Amabile and Pratt, 2016 ; Hunsaker and Ding, 2022 ). The present study, therefore, examines the BLM–IWB relationship not only as a direct behavioral association but also in relation to employees’ broader experience of work.
source_label: Leader bottom-line mentality and employees’ innovative work behavior: the role of workplace spirituality and value congruence
